result.rule: When The description opens with an actor performing a described action as its first step (for example, an organisation recognising a need), so the action is stated as work that happens after the process starts rather than as a trigger.: Model a plain start event with no action in it, then a task that carries the described opening action, performed by the responsible actor. Do not turn that action into the start event. The start event represents only the occurrence that starts the process.

When the description opens by saying that the process starts when a participant performs a named action (for example identifying a need), so that action is a performed step that precedes the first described activity: Model a plain start event with no label that carries the action. Add a task named for the participant's action, placed after the start event and before the first described activity. Route the sequence flow start event, then action task, then the first activity. Do not put the action into the start event's label, and do not drop the action because the trigger already implies it.

When the description states a performed work action at the very beginning or the very end of the process (for example, an identification step that opens the process, or one of several approval or rejection actions that closes it), and that action is described as something done rather than as a message or condition: Model each such described action as a task, placed after the start event or before the end event. Use the start event only to mark the trigger and each end event only to mark an outcome, and do not put the action's label on the event itself. When the process has several outcomes, give each outcome its own task and end event, following the stated branching.

When the description states that one step is followed by several actions that the same actor performs without a stated order, and all of them must be carried out before the process moves on: Model a parallel gateway that forks into one branch per stated action, and a parallel gateway that joins those branches before the next step. Do not connect the actions in a sequence, and do not use an exclusive gateway, because all branches must complete.
